messages.author: 13d0e40ead8b0219
messages.subject: SNPs on gigamuga array
parts:
Hi Karl,

In using your instructions for utilizing qtl2 with the DO and GigaMUGA genotyping, I used the processed GM files (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.5404750).

However, I noticed that the processed files do not contain all of the markers that are in the primary files (ftp://ftp.jax.org/MUGA).

For example, marker UNC6 is missing. The result is that if I pull markers in my cross from GM_snps (ftp://ftp.jax.org/MUGA), i get an error that not all snps are available.

cross_combined = pull_markers(cross, GM_snps_tier1_2$marker)

Warning message:
In pull_markers(cross, GM_snps_tier1_2$marker) :
  Some markers not found: UNC6, JAX00240610, JAX00000040, JAX00240691, JAX00000058, UNCJPD009367, JAX00190675, JAX00724535, JAX00241011, JAX00190683, UNCJPD009180, UNCJPD000010, UNCHS000051, UNCJPD000018, JAX00241740, UNCJPD000025, UNCHS000097, B6_01.011986786.S, UNCJPD000030, JAX00242146, JAX00190830, JAX00242170, UNCHS000110, UNCJPD000031, JAX00242373, UNCJPD000033, JAX00190858, UNCJPD009282, JAX00242691, JAX00242707, JAX00000918, JAX00242808, UNCHS000151, JAX00243092, JAX00243170, UNCJPD000047, UNCJPD000048, JAX00190966, UNCJPD000050, JAX00243620, UNCJPD000052, UNCJPD000054, UNCJPD000058, JAX00244148, UNCJPD000059, JAX00244218, UNCJPD000060, UNCJPD000061, UNCJPD000063, JAX00244376, UNCJPD000064, UNCJPD008756, UNC294157, UNC297129, JAX00244720, JAX00244775, UNCJPD000067, UNCJPD000068, UNCJPD000069, UNCJPD000070, JAX00191108, UNCJPD000071, JAX00245142, UNCJPD000075, UNCJPD000076, UNCHS000323, UNCHS000326, JAX00245377, JAX00245377r, UNCJPD000079, JAX00245378, JAX00245415, UNCJPD008793, ... <truncated>


Is there a reason that these snps are dropped within the processed GM files?

Thanks,
Basel

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] SNPs on gigamuga array
parts:
For the UN6 marker, our GigaMUGA genotypes on the founder strains has
"N" for all founders. With no usable founder genotypes the marker was
omitted.

The rest of the markers listed there are similar: either no data or all
strains have the same allele.

karl
